root_cause: Carbon monoxide poisoning from a faulty gas heater

patient.name: Maya Okafor
patient.background: Engineering student, history of migraines, lives in an old basement flat

findings.result: Carboxyhemoglobin 28%: blood carrying CO, not oxygen
Finger oxygen reading falsely normal at 99% (pulse oximetry)
Mild heart muscle strain, raised troponin
Swelling risk in deep brain areas (globus pallidus)
Empty stomach, no ulcer or bleeding (gastritis absent)
No bleed or tumor on scan (CT normal)
Liver enzymes normal, no paracetamol toxicity
Flushed pink cheeks despite illness (cherry-red tint)
Lactate raised: cells starved of oxygen (acidosis)

treatments.name: 100% oxygen, consider hyperbaric
treatments.why: High-flow oxygen pushes CO off hemoglobin, cutting its half-life from ~5 hours to ~1 hour.
treatments.attending_line: Look at that, you treated the patient instead of her migraine diary.

treatments.name: Sumatriptan for migraine
treatments.why: Triptans constrict blood vessels, further starving an oxygen-deprived heart and brain.
treatments.attending_line: Great, you squeezed her arteries shut. Her heart sends its regards.

treatments.name: Ondansetron and send home
treatments.why: Stopping the nausea hides the warning sign and sends her back into the CO-filled flat.
treatments.attending_line: Nausea fixed. Also, she's back in the gas chamber. Nice discharge.

treatments.name: Sedate with benzodiazepine
treatments.why: Sedation slows her breathing, so she clears CO even slower and drops her oxygen further.

if_wrong_cascade.text: Rising acid levels, CO stays bound

treatments.attending_line: She's calm now. Mostly because she's barely breathing.

post_mortem: Maya's old gas heater was leaking carbon monoxide, which grabs hemoglobin about 200 times more strongly than oxygen and quietly suffocates the brain and heart. The giveaways were a flatmate with the same symptoms, a headache that got better away from home, and a normal oxygen reading that can't tell CO apart from oxygen.
